prompt: Review this anchor as its assigned subagent. Enumerate ALL requirements, qualifications, edge cases and scenarios. Inspect all supplied implementation and test fragments and trace each aspect to implementation behavior and actual test assertions or justified TODO/N/A evidence. Passing tests and associations alone are insufficient. Follow helpers and capture every additional source dependency with cargo meta review read ANCHOR PATH [selector] before completing the report. Explain prerequisites for justified TODO tests; do not claim deferred behavior is implemented. Distinguish source inspection from commands actually executed. Write a JSON report containing reviewer, report, and requested_edits. Leave requested_edits empty only when every aspect is accounted for and no edits are needed. Otherwise list concrete changes, including missing tests or justified TODO tests with prerequisite comments. Run cargo meta review record ANCHOR REPORT_FILE to finish. After edits or stale-input rejection, run cargo meta review start ANCHOR and review the fresh inputs. The gate fails until a current report with no requested edits is recorded. Dependency capture is agent-declared.
coordinator_instructions:
Follow sage-review-checklist for only the assigned anchor. Begin fresh review using cargo meta review start ANCHOR --instructions /tmp/ci-anchor-review-instructions.txt. Inspect current claim, implementation, complete tests, and capture dependencies through review read. Independently assess current evidence; do not transplant old approvals. Preserve justified TODO/N/A entries honestly. Record a complete claim-specific report. Coordinate all source edits with root BEFORE editing, to avoid invalidating concurrent reviews. Prefer reporting concrete necessary changes for root to batch; do not add unrelated evidence. You own only your assigned validation directory and unique /tmp report. Distinguish source inspection from tests executed. Do not commit.
Root centrally runs relevant suites. Do not repeat full suites for a source-only review unless investigating a specific concern. Report source assessment honestly without claiming execution. This does not waive regression reproduction for suspected bugs.

substitutions, and adjustment lists into the shared calls, borrows,
dereferences, and coercions. Sage's internal method-candidate or adjustment

into a shared schema is not a license for a later pairwise normalization pass.
That fixed projection includes overloadable operators. Rustc may erase a
concrete scalar operator's type-dependent method marker before THIR, whereas
Sage deliberately keeps the semantic trait-method call through Typed IR. The
rustc emitter therefore uses the type-checked HIR operator, its resolved
operand/result types, and the corresponding language-item method signature to
emit the same resolved call and explicit adjustments. It does not identify a
concrete impl—Sage's call contract does not require one—and it does not inspect
Sage's output. This is a specified native-to-shared representation mapping,
The destination contract pairs exact textual equality with coverage
accounting. Each side reports the items and bodies in scope, including
associated and macro-generated items, and a successful comparison rejects
unsupported expression placeholders and debug-formatted fallback types. Two
emitters omitting the same body or collapsing the same expression to
`?unsupported` is not conformance. Until the general coverage validator lands,
each vertical slice must add structural checks proving that its in-scope body
is present, successfully checked, and contains no source-shaped or unsupported
nodes; textual equality alone is never accepted as evidence of coverage.

The `mini_redis/db_drop_guard.rs` fixture exercises the rule directly: rustc
projects its receiver adjustments into explicit dereference, field, and shared
borrow nodes; Sage emits its already elaborated body; and the harness decides
the result using the serialized bytes alone. Before comparison, fixture-specific
checks independently require that each side contains the source-written body
and its resolved call/borrow/field/dereference shape; these checks establish
coverage and do not rewrite either output.
The fixture also has a checked-in exact JSON snapshot. The harness requires
the independently serialized rustc output and the independently serialized
Sage output to each equal those bytes before comparing them to one another.
The snapshot is a reviewable record of the shared IR, not a normalization
input: no output is rewritten to match it. Its structural coverage assertion
also requires the external call path to be exactly `Mod → Trait → Fn`, so two
adapters cannot pass merely by repeating the same lossy kind inference.
